the burst and coast swimming mode of zebra danios is characterized by the production of a cross sectional vortex ring at the fish's tail.
the flow fields of larvae and adults are very similar in structure but that larvae experience much higher viscous effects, which lead to a very short coasting period.
larval and adult zebra danio (Brachy danio rerio) vortices are similar in shape and differ mainly in the size and circulation of their vortex cores.

the hydrodynamic effects of body size in unsteady swimming.
the flow field of fish larvae and the effects of the body size.
the hydrodynamics of fish swimming and the effect of body size on the hydrodynamic forces and flows generated by swimming fish.

the hydrodynamic effects of body size in fish are not restricted to the effects of Reynolds number on the flow regime, but that body size affects the hydrodynamics of swimming fish in a variety of ways.

the hydrodynamics of fish swimming are not only influenced by Reynolds number, but also by size.
larvae are more expensive swimmers because of their high cost of transport, which is mainly due to the large drag on the fish's body.
the flow field of larval zebra danios is dominated by viscous effects, while the flow field of adult fish is dominated by inertial effects.

larval fish swimming is fundamentally different than swimming of larger fish.
